title: KCET 2012 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect? If $a \equiv b \pmod{m}$ and $x$ is an integer, then
questions.explanation: Division is not preserved under congruence in general (need $\gcd(x,m)=1$), so $(a\div x)\equiv (b\div x)\pmod m$ can fail.

questions.q: Inverse of a diagonal non-singular matrix is a
questions.explanation: The inverse of a non-singular diagonal matrix is obtained by inverting each diagonal entry, which is again diagonal.

questions.q: If $ax^4 + bx^3 + cx^2 + dx + e = \begin{vmatrix} x^3+3x & x-1 & x+3 \\ x+1 & -2x & x-4 \\ x-3 & x+4 & 3x \end{vmatrix}$, then $e =$
questions.explanation: $e$ is the constant term, obtained by putting $x=0$: the determinant becomes $\begin{vmatrix}0&-1&3\\1&0&-4\\-3&4&0\end{vmatrix}=0$.

questions.q: If $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ are three non-coplanar vectors and $\vec p, \vec q$ and $\vec r$ are vectors defined by $\vec p = \dfrac{\vec b \times \vec c}{[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]}$, $\vec q = \dfrac{\vec c \times \vec a}{[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]}$ and $\vec r = \dfrac{\vec a \times \vec b}{[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]}$, then the value of $(\vec a + \vec b) \cdot \vec p + (\vec b + \vec c) \cdot \vec q + (\vec c + \vec a) \cdot \vec r =$
questions.explanation: $\vec p,\vec q,\vec r$ form the reciprocal system, so $\vec a\cdot\vec p=1,\vec b\cdot\vec p=\vec c\cdot\vec p=0$ (similarly for $\vec q,\vec r$). Each bracket reduces to $1$, giving a total of $3$.

questions.q: If $(\vec a \times \vec b)^2 + (\vec a \cdot \vec b)^2 = 144$ and $|\vec a| = 4$, then $|\vec b| =$
questions.explanation: Using the identity $(\vec a\times\vec b)^2+(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2$, we get $16|\vec b|^2=144$, so $|\vec b|=3$.

questions.q: Which of the following is false?
options: Set of even integers is a group under usual addition.
questions.explanation: $(N,\cdot)$ is not a group since elements other than $1$ have no multiplicative inverse in $N$.

questions.q: $2\cos^{-1}x = \sin^{-1}(2x\sqrt{1-x^2})$ is valid for all values of $x$ satisfying
questions.explanation: Writing $x=\cos\theta$, the identity $\sin^{-1}(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)=2\theta$ needs $2\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$, i.e. $\theta\in[0,\pi/4]$, which gives $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ is a complex number such that $\alpha^2 - \alpha + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha^{2011} =$
questions.explanation: $\alpha$ is a primitive 6th root of unity ($\alpha^6=1$). Since $2011=6\times335+1$, $\alpha^{2011}=\alpha$.

questions.q: If $\cos\alpha + 2\cos\beta + 3\cos\gamma = 0$, $\sin\alpha + 2\sin\beta + 3\sin\gamma = 0$ and $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = \pi$, then $\sin3\alpha + 8\sin3\beta + 27\sin3\gamma =$
questions.explanation: For $a\cos\alpha+b\cos\beta+c\cos\gamma=0$ and $a\sin\alpha+b\sin\beta+c\sin\gamma=0$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi$, we have $a^3\sin3\alpha+b^3\sin3\beta+c^3\sin3\gamma=3abc\sin(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$. Here $a{=}1,b{=}2,c{=}3$, so the value is $3(1)(2)(3)\sin\pi=0$.

questions.q: If the conjugate of $(x + iy)(1 - 2i)$ is $1 + i$, then
questions.explanation: $(x+iy)(1-2i)=\overline{1+i}=1-i$, so $x+iy=\dfrac{1-i}{1-2i}=\dfrac{3}{5}+\dfrac{1}{5}i$, giving $x=3/5,\ y=1/5$.

questions.q: If the straight line $3x + 4y = k$ touches the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16x$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.explanation: The circle $(x-8)^2+y^2=64$ has centre $(8,0)$, radius $8$. Setting $\dfrac{|24-k|}{5}=8$ gives $k=-16$ or $k=64$.

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of perpendicular tangents to the ellipse is called
questions.explanation: This locus is, by definition, the director circle of the ellipse.

questions.q: If $m\sin^{-1}x = \log_e y$, then $(1 - x^2)y'' - xy' =$
questions.explanation: Differentiating $y=e^{m\sin^{-1}x}$ twice gives the standard differential equation $(1-x^2)y''-xy'-m^2y=0$, so $(1-x^2)y''-xy'=m^2y$.

questions.q: If $y = e^{\log_e[1+x+x^2+\ldots]}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.explanation: $y=1+x+x^2+\ldots=\dfrac{1}{1-x}$ (for $|x|<1$), so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{(1-x)^2}$. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question, likely because the condition $|x|<1$ for the series to converge was not stated.

questions.q: Length of the subtangent at $(x_1, y_1)$ on $x^n y^m = a^{m+n}$, $m, n > 0$, is
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating, $y'=-\dfrac{ny}{mx}$. Subtangent $=y/y'=-\dfrac{mx}{n}$, whose magnitude is $\dfrac{m}{n}|x_1|$.

questions.q: If a ball is thrown vertically upwards and the height 's' reached in time 't' is given by $s = 22t - 11t^2$, then the total distance travelled by the ball is
questions.explanation: $v=22-22t=0$ at $t=1$, giving maximum height $s=11$. Since the ball returns to the start ($s=0$ at $t=0,2$), total distance $=2\times11=22$ units.

questions.q: The sum of two positive numbers is given. If the sum of their cubes is minimum, then
questions.explanation: With $x+y=k$ fixed, minimising $x^3+(k-x)^3$ gives $x=y=k/2$, so the numbers are equal.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} \dfrac{\sin^3x}{\sin^3x+\cos^3x}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Using $\int_a^b f(x)dx=\int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx$ with $a+b=\pi/2$, adding the integral to itself gives $2I=\pi/6$, so $I=\pi/12$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0} \dfrac{x\,2^x - x}{1-\cos x} =$
questions.explanation: $2^x-1\sim x\ln2$ and $1-\cos x\sim x^2/2$ as $x\to0$, so the limit is $\dfrac{x\cdot x\ln2}{x^2/2}=2\ln2=2\log2$.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{3x+1}{(x-1)(x+3)} = \dfrac{A}{x-1} + \dfrac{B}{x+3}$, then $\sin^{-1}\dfrac{A}{B} =$
questions.explanation: Solving gives $A=1, B=2$, so $\sin^{-1}(A/B)=\sin^{-1}(1/2)=\pi/6$.

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3 + 4x + 2 = 0$, then $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 + \gamma^3 =$
questions.explanation: Here $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0$, $\alpha\beta\gamma=-2$. When the sum of the roots is zero, $\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=3\alpha\beta\gamma=-6$.
Sum of all coefficients is $2^{10}$; removing ${}^{10}C_0$ and ${}^{10}C_{10}$ (each $=1$) leaves $2^{10}-2$.

questions.q: $p \to \sim q$ can also be written as
questions.explanation: $p\to \sim q \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q$, by the standard equivalence for implication.

questions.q: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x) = 2x + 3$, then $f^{-1}(x)$
options: does not exist because 'f' is not injective
does not exist because 'f' is not surjective
questions.explanation: $f$ is a bijection on $\mathbb R$; solving $y=2x+3$ for $x$ gives $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2}$.

questions.q: $\dfrac{\sin70^\circ + \cos40^\circ}{\cos70^\circ + \sin40^\circ} =$
questions.explanation: $\cos40^\circ=\sin50^\circ$ and $\sin40^\circ=\cos50^\circ$; using sum-to-product, the ratio simplifies to $\dfrac{2\sin60^\circ\cos10^\circ}{2\cos60^\circ\cos10^\circ}=\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The points $(11, 9)$, $(2, 1)$ and $(2, -1)$ are the midpoints of the sides of the triangle. Then the centroid is
questions.explanation: The centroid of a triangle equals the centroid of the triangle formed by its midpoints: $\left(\dfrac{11+2+2}{3},\dfrac{9+1-1}{3}\right)=(5,3)$.

questions.q: The reflection of the point $(1, 1)$ along the line $y = -x$ is
questions.explanation: Reflection of $(a,b)$ in the line $y=-x$ is $(-b,-a)$, so $(1,1)$ maps to $(-1,-1)$.

questions.q: The number of circles that touch the co-ordinate axes and the line whose slope is $-1$ and $y$-intercept is $1$, is
questions.explanation: Circles tangent to both axes have centres $(\pm r,\pm r)$. Imposing tangency to the line $x+y=1$ gives 2 valid circles with centre $(r,r)$ and 1 each with centres $(r,-r)$ and $(-r,r)$, totalling 4.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is an even function, then $f'(x)$ is
options: may be even or may be odd
questions.explanation: Differentiating $f(-x)=f(x)$ gives $-f'(-x)=f'(x)$, i.e. $f'(-x)=-f'(x)$, so $f'$ is odd.

questions.q: The perimeter of a sector is a constant. If its area is to be maximum, then the sectorial angle is
questions.explanation: With perimeter $k=2r+r\theta$ fixed, area $A=\tfrac12 r(k-2r)$; maximising over $r$ gives $r=k/4$ and then $\theta=2$ radians.

questions.q: The last digit of number $7^{886}$ is
questions.explanation: Units digit of powers of 7 cycles as $7,9,3,1$ with period 4. Since $886\equiv2\pmod4$, the last digit equals the 2nd term of the cycle, which is $9$.
By the Euclidean algorithm, $\gcd(24,92)=4=24(4)+92(-1)$, so $(m,n)=(4,-1)$.

questions.q: The characteristic equation of a matrix $A$ is $\lambda^3 - 5\lambda^2 - 3\lambda + 2 = 0$ then $|\operatorname{adj}(A)| =$
questions.explanation: Comparing with $\lambda^3-(\text{tr}A)\lambda^2+\ldots-|A|=0$ gives $|A|=-2$. For a $3\times3$ matrix, $|\operatorname{adj}A|=|A|^2=4$.

questions.q: If $\hat i + \hat j - \hat k$ and $2\hat i - 3\hat j + \hat k$ are adjacent sides of a parallelogram, then the lengths of its diagonals are
questions.explanation: Sum $=3\hat i-2\hat j$, magnitude $\sqrt{13}$; difference $=-\hat i+4\hat j-2\hat k$, magnitude $\sqrt{21}$. Diagonals are $\sqrt{21},\sqrt{13}$.

questions.q: If the volume of the parallelopiped formed by three non-coplanar vectors $\vec a, \vec b$ and $\vec c$ is 4 cubic units, then $[\vec a \times \vec b\ \ \vec b \times \vec c\ \ \vec c \times \vec a] =$
questions.explanation: $[\vec a\times\vec b\ \ \vec b\times\vec c\ \ \vec c\times\vec a]=[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c]^2=4^2=16$.

questions.q: Which of the following is a subgroup of the group $G = \{2^n \mid n \in Z\}$ under multiplication?
questions.explanation: A subgroup must be closed under inverses, so exponents must range over $Z$, not $N$; also elements $4^n=2^{2n}$ lie in $G$. Hence $\{4^n\mid n\in Z\}$ is the subgroup.

questions.q: In the group $G = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ under $\otimes_7$, the solution of $4 \otimes_7 x = 5$ is
questions.explanation: $4\times3=12\equiv5\pmod7$, so $x=3$.

questions.q: The number of real solutions of the equation $\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x(x+1)} + \sin^{-1}\sqrt{x^2+x+1} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: The domain of $\sin^{-1}\sqrt{x^2+x+1}$ requires $x(x+1)\le0$, i.e. $x\in[-1,0]$, while the square root in $\tan^{-1}$ needs $x(x+1)\ge0$; only $x=-1$ and $x=0$ satisfy both, and both check out in the original equation.

questions.q: If $\sin2x = 4\cos x$, then $x =$
questions.explanation: $2\sin x\cos x=4\cos x \Rightarrow \cos x(2\sin x-4)=0$. Since $\sin x=2$ is impossible, $\cos x=0$, whose general solution is $x=2n\pi\pm\pi/2$.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are different complex numbers with $|\beta| = 1$, then $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity: whenever $|\beta|=1$, $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|=1$.

questions.q: The equations of the two tangents from $(-5,-4)$ to the circle $x^2+y^2+4x+6y+8=0$ are
questions.explanation: Centre $(-2,-3)$, radius $\sqrt5$. Setting the distance from the centre to $y+4=m(x+5)$ equal to $\sqrt5$ gives $m=2$ or $m=-1/2$, giving the lines $2x-y+6=0$ and $x+2y+13=0$.

questions.q: If $x = t^2+2$ and $y = 2t$ represent the parametric equation of the parabola
questions.explanation: $t=y/2$, so $x=y^2/4+2 \Rightarrow y^2=4(x-2)$.

questions.q: If $x - y = 1$ is a tangent to the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{4} - \dfrac{y^2}{3} = 1$, the point of contact is
questions.explanation: For $y=mx+c$ tangent to $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, the point of contact is $\left(-\dfrac{a^2m}{c},-\dfrac{b^2}{c}\right)$. With $a^2=4,b^2=3,m=1,c=-1$, this gives $(4,3)$.

questions.q: If $y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1+x+x^2}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+2x+3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+5x+7}\right) + \ldots\ n\text{ terms}$, then $y'(0)$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1+(x+k)(x+k-1)}=\tan^{-1}(x+k)-\tan^{-1}(x+k-1)$ the sum telescopes to $y=\tan^{-1}(x+n)-\tan^{-1}x$, so $y'(0)=\dfrac{1}{1+n^2}-1=-\dfrac{n^2}{1+n^2}$. KEA awarded a grace mark, likely due to an inconsistency in the printed general term.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \sin[\pi^2]x + \cos[-\pi^2]x$ then $f'(x)$ is, here $[\pi^2]$ and $[-\pi^2]$ greatest integer function not greater than its value
questions.explanation: $[\pi^2]=9$ and $[-\pi^2]=-10$, so $f(x)=\sin9x+\cos10x$ (cosine is even), giving $f'(x)=9\cos9x-10\sin10x$.

questions.q: The tangent to the curve $xy = 25$ at any point on it cuts the coordinate axes at A and B, then the area of the triangle OAB is
questions.explanation: For $xy=c^2$, the tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ meets the axes at $(2x_1,0)$ and $(0,2y_1)$, so area $=\tfrac12(2x_1)(2y_1)=2x_1y_1=2(25)=50$.

questions.q: The length of the sub-tangent, ordinate and the sub-normal are in
questions.explanation: Subtangent $=y/y'$ and subnormal $=yy'$; their product is $y^2$, the square of the ordinate, so the three are in G.P.

questions.q: The maximum value of $xe^{-x}$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=e^{-x}(1-x)=0$ at $x=1$, giving the maximum value $f(1)=1/e$.

questions.q: If $[x]$ is the greatest integer function not greater than $x$, then $\displaystyle\int_0^{11}[x]\,dx =$
If $n \in N$ and $I_n = \displaystyle\int(\log x)^n\,dx$, then $I_n + nI_{n-1} =$
questions.explanation: Integrating by parts, $I_n=x(\log x)^n-nI_{n-1}$, so $I_n+nI_{n-1}=x(\log x)^n+c$.

questions.q: Solution of $e^{\frac{dy}{dx}} = x$ when $x = 1$ and $y = 0$ is
questions.explanation: $dy/dx=\log x$, so $y=x\log x-x+C$. Using $x=1,y=0$ gives $C=1$, so $y=x(\log x-1)+1$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x^2-(a+2)x+a}{x-2}, & x \ne 2 \\ 2, & x = 2 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 2$, then the value of $a$ is
questions.explanation: For the limit at $x=2$ to be finite, $(x-2)$ must divide the numerator, which forces $a=0$; then $f(x)=x$ near $x=2$, and the limit $2$ matches $f(2)$.

questions.q: If $\log_2(9^{x-1}+7) - \log_2(3^{x-1}+1) = 2$, then $x$ values are
questions.explanation: Let $t=3^{x-1}$; the equation becomes $\dfrac{t^2+7}{t+1}=4$, i.e. $t^2-4t+3=0$, giving $t=1$ or $t=3$, i.e. $x=1$ or $x=2$.

questions.q: If $x - 1$ is a factor of $x^5 - 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x + k = 0$, then $k$ is
questions.explanation: By the factor theorem, substituting $x=1$ must give $0$: $1-4+2-3+k=0 \Rightarrow k=4$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ have $n$ elements in common, then the number of elements common to $A 	imes B$ and $B 	imes A$ is
questions.explanation: An ordered pair lies in both $A\times B$ and $B\times A$ only if both coordinates are in $A\cap B$, giving $|A\cap B|^2=n^2$ such pairs.

questions.q: The 13th term in the expansion of $\left(x^2 + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^n$ is independent of $x$ then the sum of the divisors of $n$ is
questions.explanation: The 13th term has $r=12$: $T_{13}\propto x^{2n-2r-r}=x^{2n-3r}$. Setting $2n-36=0$ gives $n=18$. Divisors of 18 are $1,2,3,6,9,18$, summing to $39$.

questions.q: If one of the slopes of the pair of lines $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$ is $n$ times the other then
questions.explanation: With $m_1=nm_2$, $m_1+m_2=-2h/b$ and $m_1m_2=a/b$. Eliminating $m_2$ gives $4nh^2=(n+1)^2ab$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \begin{vmatrix} \sin x & \cos x & \tan x \\ x^3 & x^2 & x \\ 2x & 1 & x \end{vmatrix}$ then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0} \dfrac{f(x)}{x^2} =$
questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant and dividing by $x^2$, using $\sin x/x\to1$ and $\tan x\to0$, the limit evaluates to $-1\cdot(-1)+2\cdot1+0=1$.

questions.q: The number of solutions of the equation $z^2 + \bar z = 0$ where $z \in C$ are
questions.explanation: Writing $z=x+iy$ and separating real and imaginary parts gives $y=0$ (with $x=0,-1$) or $x=1/2$ (with $y=\pm\sqrt3/2$), a total of 4 solutions.

questions.q: The least and the greatest distances of the point $(10, 7)$ from the circle $x^2+y^2-4x-2y-20=0$ are
questions.explanation: Centre $(2,1)$, radius $5$. Distance from the point to the centre is $\sqrt{8^2+6^2}=10$, so the least and greatest distances from the circle are $10-5=5$ and $10+5=15$.
